sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT (a proposal that misses it is sent back, not scored):
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: GROMOVSWAP-L1-RQ
TITLE: Gromov-certified, curvature-gated, occupancy-preserving level-1 repair swaps on an otherwise unchanged Euclidean RQ-VAE SID
MOTIVATION: The measured failure is not that the SID is coarse; it is that behaviour neighbours are split across level-1 cells, so the true next item sits under a prefix the generator cannot reach from the context prefix (high validation L1 negative-hit rate). Four earlier rounds tried to fix this by rebuilding prefixes with curved assignment, curved centroids or curvature-controlled levels, and all failed. This idea stops rebuilding. It keeps the baseline Euclidean quantizer, keeps the level-1 cell structure, and only permits a bounded set of size-preserving swaps that are certified by a curved test and are provably non-increasing in the split-neighbour count.
NOVELTY: Hyperbolicity here is neither the assignment metric, nor a codebook-centroid update, nor a per-level curvature schedule, nor a cone. It is a CERTIFICATE FUNCTION: the four-point (Gromov) deficit measured on the training behaviour embeddings yields delta_hat, and a swap is eligible only when both items lie inside the delta_hat-thin triangle spanned by the two cell Frechet centroids. The behavioural failure count itself calibrates the pair bound (theta = logit of the measured L1 negative-hit rate), so no constant is tuned. The repair is a swap, so cell occupancy and codebook usage are conserved exactly, and the accept test is monotone (strictly decreasing) in the number of split behaviour-neighbour pairs.
CHANGE: At the end of every Stage-2 epoch, after the usual Euclidean residual argmin, a guard recomputes one hyperbolic Frechet centroid per level-1 cell, picks for each split item a destination cell from its behaviour log-ratio candidates by hyperbolic nearest centroid, pairs it with the least-compatible member of that cell, and exchanges the two level-1 codes only if the Gromov certificate holds and the swap strictly reduces split behaviour-neighbour pairs without creating new disjoint same-cell pairs. Nothing else about the quantizer, the encoder, the decoder or levels 2..L changes.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Fixed curvature c=1 Poincare ball. One-time from the Stage-2 train split: directed transition counts, popularity-adjusted PMI behaviour vectors u_i, hyperbolic behaviour embeddings b_i = tanh(||u_i||/tau) u_i/||u_i|| with tau = median ||u_i||, symmetric pair log-ratio A_ij, and delta_hat = median four-point deficit over 1e5 seeded quadruples. Guard off for the first 300 epochs (10% of the frozen 3000), at which point p_neg = train-split level-1 negative-hit rate of that pre-guard partition and theta = log((1-p_neg)/p_neg) are frozen for the rest of the run. From then on, once per epoch: recompute Karcher means m_c (5 iterations), for each split item i take C_i = {code1(j) : A_ij >= theta, j in Nbr(i)}, c* = argmin_{c in C_i} d_H(b_i,m_c), partner k = argmax_{k in cell(c*)} [G(k,a) - G(k,c*)], certify e_i and e_k against delta_hat, compute exact dS and dD over the union of the two cells' neighbour lists, and swap only if dS < 0 and dD <= 0. Swapped items are pinned at level 1 for the next epoch and then released. Everything is deterministic given a seed."}
COST: One-time precompute: sparse counts/PMI over 24556 items with at most 128 stored neighbours each (~3.1e6 entries) plus delta_hat over 1e5 quadruples (6e5 Poincare distances) = under 2 minutes of CPU, once. Per epoch: 256 Karcher means x 5 iterations x ~96 members (~8e7 flops) plus a guard pass of |V| <= 24556 items, each doing <=128 neighbour counts and ~96 cell-mate log-ratio lookups for dS/dD (~4.7e6 sparse lookups), vectorised to roughly 0.15-0.5 s per epoch on CPU/GPU, i.e. 8-25 minutes extra across 3000 epochs, +3-8% wall clock on four cards. Amortised per training step at 24 steps per epoch this is 6-20 ms, under 2% of a step. No new trainable parameters, no extra backward pass, no change to the 24556-item codebook update cost.
HYPOTHESIS: The idea is worth keeping only if the level-1 prefix is the bottleneck: then the certified swaps must lower the validation L1 negative-hit rate below the frozen train p_neg and raise the predictability of the true next SID's first token, which should show up as Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065. Observation: per-epoch S (split pair count) must be non-increasing by construction, the accepted-swap count must fall to near zero as training converges, and the validation L1 negative-hit rate must move in the same direction as recall.
RISKS: ['(a) The certificate or the dS<0 rule may certify almost nothing, making the mechanism inert and reproducing the baseline numbers; (b) swaps may damage per-item reconstruction so much that the encoder and the level-1 codebook degrade, hurting prefix quality; (c) p_neg measured at epoch 300 may be dominated by warm-up noise, making theta too lenient and dD almost vacuous; (d) the recall bottleneck may be at levels 2-3 rather than level 1, in which case a level-1-only repair cannot help; (e) one seed only, so a small positive or negative effect is inside seed noise.']
END IDEA

IDEA: HEXSWAP-SID
TITLE: Curvature-gated, size-preserving exchange repair of the level-1 RQ-VAE token using training-only transition log-ratios and Lorentz geodesic bisectors.
MOTIVATION: The measured failure is not that the RQ-VAE codebook is badly placed; it is that the level-1 cell of an item contains behaviourally disjoint items, so a Stage-3 sampler that commits to a coarse token is forced into a candidate set whose members have nothing to do with the anchor. Earlier rounds attacked this by re-placing codewords (Frechet means), re-scaling curvature per prefix level, or re-ranking the assignment radially by context entropy, and none produced the required drop in the level-1 negative hit rate. This idea accepts the learned codebooks and the learned cell sizes as given and only repairs the membership of a small, explicitly admissible set of items, so the diagnostic cannot be improved by shrinking cells.
NOVELTY: It is a post-quantization discrete repair, not a codebook update, not a curvature schedule, and not a radial re-weighting. Three properties are new here: (i) level-1 cell cardinalities are provably invariant (every accepted action is a two-item exchange), so the L1 negative-hit diagnostic is attributable to cell composition alone; (ii) the move set is generated only where the Lorentz nearest codeword disagrees with the frozen Euclidean RQ-VAE assignment, so the geometry does quantizer work rather than decorating it; (iii) admissibility is a single inequality in which the behaviour log-ratio must overcome a curvature-scaled bisector penalty, plus a lexicographic potential that is monotone non-increasing by construction. Unmoved items keep byte-identical baseline SIDs.
CHANGE: After the 3000th Stage-2 epoch and before SIDs are frozen for Stage 3, embed the frozen item latents and the frozen level-1 codewords into the Lorentz model with curvature derived from the measured Gromov delta of the training transition graph, and greedily execute item exchanges between Lorentz-geodesically adjacent level-1 cells whose behaviour log-ratio clears a bound tau taken from the quantile of the baseline same-cell log-ratios at 1 minus the baseline train-split L1 negative-hit rate. Each exchange is taken only if the behaviour-conditioned, curvature-scaled admissibility margin is positive and the pair potential (number of behaviour-disjoint geodesically adjacent cell pairs, number of behaviour-disjoint same-cell pairs) decreases lexicographically; residuals at levels 2 and 3 are re-quantized only for the moved items.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'See SPEC EQUATIONS. Symbols: N = 24556 items, W the symmetrised training transition matrix, d_i its degree, M = sum(W)/2, alpha = 2M/(N(N-1)) the configuration-model edge expectation (fallback 1 if M = 0), lambda_ij the popularity-adjusted transition log-ratio, rho_ab the cell-pair version of it, K the curvature, x_i and c_a the Lorentz images of item latent and codeword, d_L the Lorentz distance, m the signed bisector margin. Bound tau is the (1 - h1_train) empirical quantile of the baseline same-L1 pair log-ratios, where h1_train is the baseline L1 negative hit rate estimated on the training split. No constant is chosen by trying values: alpha, K and tau are all measured or derived quantities.'}
COST: Stage 2 and Stage 3 are untouched: 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 optimizer steps, added per-step cost exactly 0. The repair is one post-hoc pass: transition-graph build O(nnz(D_train)), Lorentz Voronoi adjacency over C1=256 codewords at 3 geodesic probes and d=64, about 3.2e9 flops (well under one second on the four cards already allocated, about 20 s on CPU); item candidates at most N x mean degree about 1.5e5 distance evaluations; residual re-quantization O(#moves x d x (|C2|+|C3|)), bounded by 24556 x 64 x 512 in the impossible worst case and in practice a few thousand items. Total added wall clock on the order of one minute, under 0.5 percent of the run; amortized over the frozen 72000 steps this is roughly 1e4 flops per step, below 0.1 percent of a training step.
HYPOTHESIS: The idea is worth keeping only if, in the single coupled run, the validation L1 negative hit rate falls below the baseline value at unchanged level-1 cell sizes, the Stage-3 level-1 token accuracy rises, and test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065. Pre-registered kill conditions: if the baseline h1 (train estimate) is below 0.02 the cell contents are already coherent and no exchange can help; if the Lorentz nearest-codeword disagrees with the Euclidean assignment for fewer than 100 items the curvature term is inert and the result must be recorded as a geometry no-op, not as a negative on the mechanism.
RISKS: ['The frozen encoder latent may be near-Euclidean at the measured curvature, making the Lorentz-versus-Euclidean disagreement set empty and the repair a no-op; the tau quantile may be so high that no swap is admissible and the SID file is unchanged; swapping an item out of the cell the encoder chose breaks encoder-SID consistency and could cost reconstruction quality that Stage 3 partly relies on; the improvement may be confined to level 1 while L2/L3 negative hits dominate the recall loss; a single run with one seed cannot separate a small true gain from seed noise, so only a clear h1 drop plus a recall above 0.065 is interpretable.']
END IDEA

IDEA: HYP-CERT-LEAFREPAIR
TITLE: Prefix-preserving, certificate-gated hyperbolic repair of the deepest SID code, scored by a behaviour-displaced Poincaré point
MOTIVATION: The measured Stage-3 failure is not a bad prefix tree but a bad local partition: behaviourally coherent items are split across cells while behaviourally disjoint items share a cell, and every previous attempt fixed it by rebuilding prefixes, which the last four rounds falsified. Stage 3 consumes only the item->SID tuple, so the map must move, but it can move in exactly one coordinate: the deepest code. This idea repairs only that coordinate, only where a training-split certificate proves the move cannot add a cross-cell coherent pair or a same-cell disjoint pair, and leaves levels 1..L-1 bit-identical.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds changed the codebook (Poincaré--Fréchet successor updates), the curvature schedule (CURVCTRL per-level curvature from prefix-transition scores), the radial coordinate of assignment (BRad-RQ context-entropy radius), or re-solved the assignment wholesale. This changes none of those: the codebooks, the encoder, the metric of the quantizer and the prefix partition are frozen; the only mutable object is the last-level token of a certified subset of items, and the decision score is a product of a training-transition agreement term with a Poincaré distance measured from a behaviour-displaced point (a hyperbolic gyromidpoint of the item with its behavioural neighbours), not a Voronoi re-assignment.
CHANGE: After Stage-2 epoch 3000, one deterministic pass re-assigns the last RQ level only, scoring each candidate code by q_behaviour(k') * exp(-d_kappa(v_i, c_k)), where v_i is the curved behaviour-displaced position of item i; a move is taken only if a train-split admissibility certificate (no increase in split coherent neighbours, no increase in same-cell disjoint neighbours) plus a cell-radius geometric guard both pass.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "(1) From TRAIN sequences only, count directed consecutive pairs, symmetrise n_ij, form the popularity-adjusted log-ratio LR(i,j)=ln(n_ij*2N_pair/((n_i+1)(n_j+1))). Neighbourhood N(i) = top-M_i by n_ij where M_i is the smallest prefix covering 90% of item i's transition mass, capped at the measured 95th percentile of that M distribution. Weights w_ij=max(0,LR(i,j)), normalised to w_hat. (2) Measure the baseline's TRAIN-split L1 negative-hit rate r0 with the same estimator used as diagnostic, and fix the coherence bound B=ln((1-r0)/r0). (3) Curvature: unit Poincaré ball, kappa=1 (fixed negative curvature, curvature radius 1). For item i, r_i = z_i - mu_{p(i)} (frozen Stage-2 encoder output minus its frozen prefix-centroid), scale s = 7.6 / max_i||r_i|| (derived from artanh(1-1e-3)). Anchor a=phi(mu_{p(i)}); u_i = exp^kappa_a(s*r_i); c_k = exp^kappa_a(s*c^(L)_k); v_i = gyromidpoint of {u_i} U {u_j : j in N(i)} with weights {1} U {w_hat_ij}. (4) Candidates C_i = distinct a_j^L over j in N(i), excluding a_i^L. (5) Accept at most one move per item, processed in decreasing transition-mass order, exactly once, with the certificate of the SPEC EQUATIONS block."}
COST: Zero added Stage-2 optimizer steps and zero added Stage-3 cost: 3000 epochs x 24 = 72,000 Stage-2 steps and the frozen 150-epoch Stage-3 protocol are unchanged, same token vocabulary and same sequence lengths. The repair pass is one shot after epoch 3000: graph build O(total train transitions), then 24,556 items x M_i neighbours (M_i typically 50-150) gyromidpoint iterations (10 Ungar steps) plus <= |C_i| <= 256 Poincaré distances: worst case about 5.7e8 scalar ops plus 3.7e6 integer certificate operations, under 2 minutes on one card if the per-item candidate block is vectorised, i.e. under 0.1% of Stage-2 wall clock and an amortised equivalent of about 1.7 ms per Stage-2 step at the frozen scale. Memory: one |I| x M_i index/weight block plus 24,556 x d ball coordinates.
HYPOTHESIS: The recall loss is concentrated in last-token confusion among behaviourally coherent items whose text residuals sit where curvature distorts the comparison; if so, moving them must lower the validation L1 negative-hit rate while leaving every prefix token fixed, and Stage-3 test recall@10 must exceed 0.065 with a measurable fraction of moved items (expected single-digit percent). It is worth keeping only if (a) at least a few hundred moves are certified, (b) validation negRate@L1 falls, and (c) test recall@10 > 0.065; otherwise the no-op / small-move outcome is recorded with its numbers as a negative result.
RISKS: ["The candidate set C_i is built from neighbours' leaf codes, so items whose behavioural neighbours all live under different prefixes may yield no admissible move and the mechanism degenerates to an exact no-op (recall identical to baseline). The certificate may bind almost everywhere and admit only a handful of moves, giving no measurable effect. The cell-radius guard can veto precisely the boundary items the mechanism targets. Changing the last token for a few items perturbs Stage-3's last-level token statistics, which could cost more than it gains. The disjointness objective may be only weakly correlated with next-item recall. Fixed kappa=1 with data-driven scaling means the geometric term may be nearly Euclidean in effect, making the geometry-off comparison numerically close even though the code path differs."]
END IDEA

IDEA: ADM-GEO-RQ
TITLE: Admissible geodesic re-assignment: a curved distance budget gated by a measured behaviour-disjoint-pair veto
MOTIVATION: The measured failure is that the RQ-VAE places items in the same prefix even when their training behaviour is disjoint, so the Stage-3 generator spends prefix probability on items the user would never transition to. Earlier rounds attacked this by moving codebook positions (curved Frechet means), by changing the curvature value per level, or by re-scoring radius/assignment to build new prefixes; all rebuilt the partition and all failed. The remaining failure mode is the assignment step itself: it is unconstrained on the negative side. This idea keeps the baseline partition, the codebook positions and the Euclidean training losses, and constrains only individual re-assignment moves with (i) a hard behaviour veto that can never increase same-prefix behaviour-disjoint pairs and (ii) a hyperbolic travel budget that says how far an item may move to join a behaviour-coherent cell.
NOVELTY: Not a codebook update (rejects poincare-frechet-successor-codebook), not a curvature schedule (rejects CURVCTRL-SID), not a radius/entropy assignment score (rejects BRad-RQ), not a new-prefix rebuild (rejects the whole last four rounds). It is a monotone admissibility operator on the discrete assignment: the curved metric appears only as the permitted travel budget inside an inequality, and the behaviour graph appears only as the negative-side count inside the same inequality, so neither can act without the other. The bound tau is self-calibrated from the baseline's own measured negative-hit rate, so no constant is tuned.
CHANGE: At each RQ level, instead of taking the nearest code outright, item i may move from its current code a to a candidate code b only if (1) the number of behaviour-disjoint items already in b (with the same shorter prefix) does not exceed the number in a, and (2) the Poincare distance increase from a to b is at most a behaviour-derived allowance scaled by a measured code-to-code Poincare scale. Otherwise the item stays where it is.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Let D be the RQ depth (e.g. 3), K the codebook size per level, d the residual dimension. Epoch 0 is the ordinary text-embedding RQ-VAE with no behaviour term and yields the initial assignment A0(i,l) = Euclidean argmin code at level l.\nStep 1 (train-only behaviour graph). From TRAIN sequences count consecutive in-session directed transitions N_ij and symmetrise A_ij = N_ij + N_ji. Popularity-adjusted score s_ij = log( (A_ij + 1) / (deg_i deg_j / (2M) + 1) ), where deg is the symmetrised weighted degree and M the number of undirected edges (Laplace +1 is a documented default, not a tuned value). Behaviour-disjoint means s_ij <= 0. Keep for each item its top-64 neighbours by s as the sparse support of the veto (cap equal to the baseline context length, not tuned).\nStep 2 (derived constants, all from TRAIN at epoch 0). h0 = fraction of same-L1-cell item pairs with s_ij <= 0 (the baseline negative hit rate, TRAIN only). Pos = { s_ij : s_ij > 0 and i,j share the L1 cell at epoch 0 }. tau = Quantile over Pos at probability q = h0, so a worse baseline demands stronger coherence; no tuning. rho_l = RMS norm of the epoch-0 level-l code vectors (measured, sets the exp-map scale so residuals do not saturate the ball). lambda_l = median pairwise Euclidean distance among epoch-0 level-l code vectors (measured, scales the allowance). Curvature K = 1, fixed, documented default; the Gromov delta of the TRAIN transition metric is recorded as a diagnostic only and never sets K.\nStep 3 (curved images). phi_l(x) = exp^K_0(x / rho_l). For item i, u_i = phi_l(residual_l(i)); for code c, v_c = phi_l(c_l). dP(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2K||u-v||^2 / ((1-K||u||^2)(1-K||v||^2))) / sqrt(K).\nStep 4 (admission). For item i at level l with a = A(i,l), order all K codes by dP ascending and take the first m = D candidates (m equals the RQ depth, not tuned). For each candidate b != a compute created = number of j in Supp_i with s_ij <= 0, A(j,l) = b and prefix_{<l}(j) = prefix_{<l}(i); removed = same count for a; dX = created - removed; sbar_i(b) = mean of s_ij over the items j already in cell b sharing the shorter prefix (tau if cell b is empty); allowance = lambda_l * max(0, sbar_i(b) - tau); gap = dP(u_i, v_b) - dP(u_i, v_a). Admit iff dX <= 0 AND gap <= allowance; among admitted candidates take the smallest gap; apply with straight-through. Codebook positions, reconstruction loss and commitment loss stay exactly as in the baseline.\nStep 5: nothing else changes. Decoder, Stage-2 schedule, Stage-3 protocol, seed: frozen.'}
COST: Per step (batch 1024, D=3, K=256, d=32): the K-code distance evaluations already exist in the baseline argmin, now in the curved metric; add 1024*3*3 = 9216 Poincare distances (~30 flops each) and 1024*3*3*20 = 184320 sparse neighbour lookups for the veto against a precomputed boolean disjoint-edge matrix. About 3e5 flops per step, 2-4 ms batched on GPU, under 3 percent of a step whose transformer decoder forward dominates; overhead over 72000 steps (24 steps x 3000 epochs) is a few GPU minutes. One-off CPU: build the top-64 graph and the boolean veto matrix (24556 items, ~1.5e6 entries, 2-5 min), measure h0, tau, rho_l, lambda_l once at epoch 0 (~1 min). No new parameters; extra memory is the sparse veto matrix (~6 MB int32).
HYPOTHESIS: If the failure really is same-prefix/disjoint-behaviour, the veto plus the curved budget rejects a few high-damage baseline moves and admits a few behaviour-coherent ones: SID churn stays between 3 and 15 percent (partition nearly the baseline), the validation L1 negative hit rate falls clearly below its epoch-0 value, and Stage-3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 because the generator no longer spends prefix mass on disjoint items. If churn is ~0 the mechanism is inert on this pathway; if churn is large and the negative hit rate does not fall it is the same failure again and is recorded as such.
RISKS: ['(1) The dX <= 0 veto can be satisfied trivially by staying put, making the operator inert and Stage 3 bit-identical to baseline - visible in the admitted-move counters. (2) h0 near 1 makes tau strict and leaves only zero-allowance moves, again near-inert. (3) For small residual norms the exp map is nearly linear, so geometry-off and both-on coincide; the mean dP / mean L2 ratio is reported, and a ratio within 1 percent means the result must be recorded as a geometry failure, not a behaviour failure. (4) The straight-through gradient stays Euclidean, so the encoder can drift and later reassign the same pairs; the veto is re-evaluated each step, so this shows up as oscillation, bounded but not eliminated by the no-move-unless-admitted rule. (5) A frozen 150-epoch Stage 3 may be insensitive to a small SID change, so a true effect may be unobservable in one run.']
END IDEA

IDEA: TAUSWAP-POINCARE-EXCHANGE
TITLE: Cardinality-preserving Poincare-selected level-1 prefix exchange, admitted only by a measured negative-hit budget
MOTIVATION: The measured failure is not a bad codebook, it is a small set of level-1 prefix cells that hold items whose training behaviour is disjoint; every predicted-prefix collision with a behaviourally unrelated item is a miss the tail tokens cannot repair. Earlier rounds attacked this by re-quantising (new prefixes, Frechet codebook updates, per-level curvature control) and were falsified. This keeps the partition, codebooks, encoder and decoder intact and repairs only the empirical collision set, using curved behaviour geometry to choose which items trade cells.
NOVELTY: The curved operation never touches the quantizer, the residual levels or the training loss; it acts only inside a post-Stage-2 exchange operator. That exchange is (a) cardinality preserving, so the prefix vocabulary, prefix frequencies and cell-size profile of the baseline are exactly unchanged, (b) capped at one move per item, and (c) admitted by exact integer counts on both sides of the partition (disjoint same-cell pairs and split behaviour-neighbour pairs) whose threshold is the baseline's measured negative-hit rate, not a swept constant. Prior candidates changed the assignment rule itself; this changes who sits in which cell, for a measured few items, and nothing else.
CHANGE: After the last Stage-2 epoch, build behaviour points u_i in the unit Poincare ball from PMI-compressed transition profiles, compute each frozen level-1 cell's hyperbolic Frechet mean, then greedily execute 1-for-1 cell exchanges whose behaviour-weighted Poincare gain is positive and whose exact Delta-D / Delta-R counts satisfy the admissibility predicate; only the tail tokens of moved items are re-derived, with the frozen level-2/3 codebooks.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'Inputs: frozen RQ-VAE codebooks (levels 1..3), frozen per-item SIDs, training-split directed transition counts C with internal-holdout edges deleted, training-user internal holdout pairs. Steps: (1) r(i,j)=log((C_ij+1)/(T p_i q_j +1)); (2) h0 = measured internal negative-hit rate, tau = h0-quantile of r over all same-level-1 pairs; (3) z_i = 32-dim truncated SVD coordinates of the non-negative PMI row; (4) u_i = tanh(c||z_i||) z_i/||z_i||, c = 1/median||z||; (5) m_b = Karcher mean of cell b; (6) enumerate candidate swaps i in a, k in b where b contains a behaviour neighbour of i; (7) greedy accept in decreasing G under the admissibility predicate and the |S_neg| cap; (8) re-encode tails of moved items; (9) emit SIDs and diagnostics. Output: patched SID table with identical prefix vocabulary and identical cell-size multiset, plus h1, the moved list, and Delta-D / Delta-R ledgers.'}
COST: Zero added cost in all 72,000 Stage-2 steps (24 steps/epoch x 3000 epochs) and no change to the frozen 150-epoch Stage-3 protocol. One-time repair after epoch 3000: randomized truncated SVD of 24556 x 24556 with about 5e5 nonzeros (dominant term, 1-3 min on one card), 256 Karcher means x 15 iterations x ~96 members x 32 dims = 1.2e7 FLOPs, candidate gains about 5e7 FLOPs, gate counting about 1e7 integer ops, about 3 MB dense plus the sparse graph. Total under 5 minutes, roughly the wall clock of 5-10 Stage-2 epochs; no per-step recurrence.
